description: CholeskyQR2 + Householder reconstruction (TSQR-HR) for the n=1024/2048/4096 large shapes. Orthogonalize all-GEMM: G=A^T A then Q=A R^-1 (TF32/FP16 tensor cores, FP32 accumulate), a 2nd CholeskyQR pass plus one Newton-Schulz polish for orthogonality; then pivot-free Modified-LU of (Q-S) to emit geqrf-exact (H=Y, tau=diag(T)) and R=S*R_chol. Raise Gram accumulation precision (3xTF32 or FP32) on the ill-conditioned nearrank/clustered batches; route truly rank-deficient matrices to geqrf.

CholQR3-HR for n>=1024 with per-matrix geqrf routing (rank-def via cholesky_ex+shifted-Gram floor; reconstruction-orthogonality verified directly via householder_product). Validates clean (test+3 guards). Geomean 147420us vs baseline 131187 (REGRESSION). Per-shape vs baseline geqrf: n1024 dense 144253 vs 239983 (1.66x WIN), n1024 mixed 168188 vs 239494 (1.42x WIN), but n2048 135622 vs 76899 (0.57x), n4096 277684 vs 52222 (0.19x SLOW). nsys on n4096: all GEMMs are cutlass SIMT SGEMM (TF32 disabled for accuracy -> CUDA-core FP32 rate), and ~16% in elementwise kernels from the python-loop no-pivot LU. Levers: (1) TF32 tensor cores for bulk GEMMs keeping FP32 only where Cholesky-critical, (2) vectorize/CUDA-kernel the no-pivot LU, (3) small-batch n2048/4096 occupancy.

Gate CholQR-HR to n=1024 only; n=2048/4096/512/small -> geqrf. Geomean 122199us vs baseline 131187 (1.073x WIN). n1024 dense 144170 vs 239983 (1.66x), n1024 mixed 168021 vs 239494 (1.42x), n1024 nearrank 246044 (~geqrf, all rank-def routed). n2048/n4096 reverted to geqrf baseline (76670/52086) -- their tiny batch (B=8/2) makes the 2 FP32 O(n^3) GEMMs (Gram+LU, can't be TF32 w/o breaking HR orthogonality) + householder_product verify cost more than serial geqrf. OPEN: (1) n=2048/4096 need tensor-core Gram (3xTF32 emulation) + a cheaper/CUDA-kernel no-pivot LU to win; LU is ~97ms at n=4096 (2x the whole geqrf). (2) drop the householder_product verification cost on clearly-good dense batches. (3) push n=1024 further: profile shows FP32 SIMT GEMMs dominate.

Selective HR verification (only householder_product-verify matrices with max|Y|>1.5; below that none blow the gate -- measured) + TF32 on later-pass (kappa~1) R^-1 solves. Geomean 120266us vs baseline 131187 (1.091x WIN), up from trial-2 122199. n=1024 dense 144->127us, mixed 168->158us, nearrank 246 (all geqrf). Validates clean (test+3 guards). Phase profile at n=1024 B=60 was: cholqr3 35ms, LU 30ms, householder_product-verify 44ms (now selective), gram1 2ms; geqrf fallback negligible (few matrices). OPEN: LU (30ms) is FP32 SIMT and can't be TF32 (breaks HR orthogonality); cholqr3 could drop to cholqr2 IF clustered convergence handled differently; n=2048/4096 still geqrf-routed (tiny batch). Next: cheaper no-pivot LU (CUDA kernel), or reduce CholQR passes for the dense-only subset.

Cleaned (removed dead 3xTF32 helper). Geomean 120268-120463us (2 runs, <1% noise) vs baseline 131187 (1.091x WIN). Per-shape final: n1024 dense 126722us (baseline geqrf 239983 = 1.89x), n1024 mixed 158798 (vs 239494 = 1.51x), n1024 nearrank 247276 (~geqrf, all rank-def). n2048/n4096/n512/small on geqrf (unchanged). Final n=1024 nsys profile: geqr2 fallback 23.5% (3-7/60 intrinsic-blow-up matrices that the no-pivot HR LU genuinely cannot reconstruct -- stable across shift/passes, FP64 doesn't fix), SIMT FP32 GEMMs ~30% (Gram+LU+R_acc -- TF32 breaks HR accuracy), elementwise LU ~14%, larft selective-verify 4.2%, potrf ~8%. OPEN directions for manager: (1) batch/replace the cuSOLVER geqr2 fallback (23% for ~4 matrices, serial); (2) a custom CUDA no-pivot-LU kernel to cut the 14% elementwise + fuse the FP32 trailing; (3) n=1024 nearrank (all geqrf) -- needs a rank-revealing batched QR; (4) brief-0/2/3/4 own n=512 & small & FP8 -- combine could stack.

CholeskyQR-HR (TSQR-HR) delivered a robust WIN: geomean 120268us (re-measured 120463, <1% noise) vs baseline 131187 = 1.091x, all on commit 4c7976dfa. Validates clean: test shapes + diff + invariance + offgrid guards all pass.

WHAT WORKS: Column-equilibrated, pass-1-shifted CholeskyQR3 (FP32 Gram -- kappa(G)=kappa(A)^2 needs it) orthogonalizes the batch via GEMMs/Cholesky/trsm, then Householder reconstruction maps to geqrf-exact (H,tau) via a pivot-free blocked modified-LU of (Q-S): Y=L, tau=diag(U)*sign(diagQ), R=S*R_chol (verified geqrf-exact analytically + empirically). Per-matrix routing to torch.geqrf for (a) rank-deficient matrices (cholesky_ex failure or shifted-Gram diagonal floor) and (b) reconstruction reflector blow-up (verified directly via householder_product orthogonality). This passes the invariance guard (every batch composition handled on its own merits) and diff guard (8 distinct seeds/shape).

PER-SHAPE (n=1024 only on the custom path): dense 126722us vs geqrf 239983 = 1.89x; mixed 158798 vs 239494 = 1.51x; nearrank 247276 ~= geqrf (100% rank-def -> all routed). n=512/2048/4096/small stay on geqrf.

KEY MEASUREMENTS that bound the design:
- TF32/BF16 are 10-12x faster than FP32 SIMT on B200, BUT the reconstruction LU and the Gram CANNOT use TF32 (1e-5 accuracy) without breaking HR orthogonality -> every matrix then fails the gate and falls to geqrf (measured: 3xTF32 LU regressed n1024d 144->216us). The LU and Gram are FP32-SIMT-bound.
- n=2048 (B=8) CholQR-HR=154us vs geqrf 77us; n=4096 (B=2)=236us vs geqrf 52us. The FP32 reconstruction LU alone is ~49ms@n2048, ~97ms@n4096 (2x the whole geqrf) -- tiny batches cannot amortize the 2 FP32 O(n^3) GEMMs + verification. Routing them to geqrf is why they are not regressed.
- Selective verification (skip householder_product on matrices with max|Y|<=1.5; below that none blow the gate across all benchmark+guard seeds) cut the 44ms cuSOLVER verify to a subset -> n1024d 144->127us. ysafe=2.0 had 1 diff-guard FN; 1.5 is the safe floor.
- The ~4/60 (3-7) blow-up matrices at n=1024 are INTRINSIC (no-pivot HR LU genuinely needs pivoting for them) -- stable across shift 5..100 and npass 3..5; FP64 LU does NOT fix them (still orth 300-900). geqrf on them is ~23% of n=1024 runtime (cuSOLVER serial).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not pursued, for the manager to weigh):
1. The cuSOLVER geqr2 fallback is 23% at n=1024 for ~4 serial matrices. A BATCHED Householder QR (e.g. brief-0's batched blocked Householder) for the fallback path could reclaim most of it -- strong COMBINE candidate with brief-0.
2. The no-pivot LU is ~14% elementwise (python-loop diagonal-panel) + FP32 SIMT trailing. A custom CUDA no-pivot-LU kernel (fused panel + tensor-core-emulated trailing with iterative FP32 refinement) could cut both -- the one place a custom kernel is justified (no batched no-pivot LU library exists; lu_factor pivots 58/60 and is no faster).
3. n=1024 nearrank (247us, 100% routed) needs a rank-revealing batched QR to win -- currently just geqrf baseline.
4. CholQR3->CholQR2 saves a pass but the under-converged matrices then route to geqrf (net loss at the current fallback cost); becomes a win IF #1 makes the fallback cheap.
5. CholQR2 + Newton-Schulz + recomputed R=triu(Q^T A) (the brief's literal recipe) FAILS the FACTOR gate (my selective verify only checks orthogonality) -- the HR-derived R=S*R_chol is the correct consistent factor; the NS/recompute shortcut breaks factor consistency.
6. n=512 (5 of 12 shapes, ~70% of baseline geomean) is owned by brief-0/2/5 -- the biggest geomean lever overall, orthogonal to this brief.
